cultivar: Original seedlings with some newer clonals
processing: Orthodox Darjeeling processing, with lighter oxidation in spring as is usual for the district. Organically grown since the 1990s according to sellers' accounts.
harvest_season: Offered in first flush, second flush and autumn lots; spring and summer pickings are the most commonly seen.
appearance_dry: Typical of Darjeeling, wiry olive-and-brown leaf with some pale tips in higher grades, darker in summer and autumn.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in first flush, deeper amber in second flush and autumn.
appearance_wet: Small, supple green-and-copper leaf in spring, browner later.
taste_profile: Tasting records are mostly from sellers. As with other China-leaning Darjeelings, expect a floral, brisk spring cup and a rounder, fruitier summer and autumn cup.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Use about 85°C for first flush and hotter water for autumn lots.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush with lot numbers, for example first flush FTGFOP1 and second flush TGBOP grades on dated invoices. First flush is best within about a year; second flush and autumn hold somewhat longer.
description:
Seeyok sits at the top end of the Mirik Valley, close to the Nepalese border. It is one of the Darjeeling names you will actually find on shop shelves, sold by flush and invoice.

The bushes are a mix: original seedlings still producing, with clonals added more recently. Sellers give an altitude range of roughly 1,000 to 1,800 metres, and describe the garden as organic since the 1990s.

Expect what a China-leaning Darjeeling usually gives: flowers and briskness in spring, ripe fruit in summer and autumn. Brew spring lots cooler and shorter than you would a normal black tea.

The invoice number and grade are useful when buying. Whole-leaf grades like FTGFOP1 suit a slow pot, while broken grades like TGBOP brew faster and stronger.
history: Most accounts give 1869 as the founding year, though this rests on sellers' descriptions rather than an estate record. The dates given for the switch to organic growing vary: 1994 in one account, simply the 1990s in others.
